kinds.d: Fresh truffle, species ordered by value.

x.d: Tuber magnatum, from Langhe and Monferrato (Alba, Asti) and Molise; sells for thousands of dollars per pound.
Tuber melanosporum, second most valuable, harvested late autumn and winter.
Tuber uncinatum, autumn truffle with darker aromatic flesh, same species as T. aestivum.
Tuber aestivum, black summer truffle found across Europe.
Tuber borchii, whitish truffle of Tuscany and Umbria, less aromatic.
Terfezia and Tirmania of Africa and the Middle East; used by Romans mainly as a flavour carrier.

kinds.d: Fresh Tricholoma matsutake, Japanese premium autumn mushroom.

x.d: Tricholoma matsutake with Pinus densiflora in Japan; domestic harvest now under 1,000 tons and imports supply most of the market.
Matsutake of Longjing City, Jilin, 'Hometown of Matsutake'.

kinds.d: Fresh porcini or cep (Boletus edulis group); dried is in Pantry Staples.

x.d: Porcini of the Borgotaro area near Parma, PGI, covering four Boletus species.

kinds.d: Fresh morel; dried morels are in Pantry Staples.

notes: Tanba/Yangyang/Tibet matsutake origins not on retrieved page (replaced by Japanese and Jilin). Chinese winter truffle not found. Chanterelle/morel types from Wikipedia.
